title: Sort the front-row items into the crate and onto the tray (Unitree G1, fixed pelvis, Pink IK)
text:
A work table holds a colourful spread of fruits, vegetables and household items, with an open blue plastic crate on one side and a round serving tray on the other.
Goal: bus the table, SORTED. Move every fruit and vegetable that sits in the front working row — a lemon, and another lemon — into the blue crate, and move the non-food items from that row — a lime, and another lime — onto the round tray. Items further back on the table are part of the scene and stay where they are. The job is done when each listed item rests in its correct destination and nothing that is not food has been put in the crate.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run both yellow lemons of the front working row (its two right-hand items) [lemon_a, lemon_b] are in the blue crate on the robot's right. Each lemon's origin (at its base), in the crate's frame, is within ±0.1043 m along the table's width and ±0.0788 m along its depth of the crate's base centre, and 0.012-0.1739 m above the crate's base. Both green limes of that row (its two left-hand items) [lime_a, lime_b] are on the round tray on the robot's left: origin within 0.0896 m horizontally of the tray's geometric centre and 0-0.1731 m above the tray's base. All four move slower than 0.06 m/s. None of the five non-food items (milk jug, white bottle, crab pen holder, utility jug, serving bowl) has its origin inside that crate box, whatever its speed. The crate stands upright, up-axis within 56.95° of vertical; it is fixed, so this always holds. Other produce in the crate does not matter. Not true at the start.
